questions.q: What single rule defines whether a reconnaissance technique counts as "passive"?
options: Whether the tool used is free versus commercial
Whether the technique is performed during business hours
Whether the data gathered is publicly indexed by Google
Whether any packet is sent directly to infrastructure the target owns or controls
questions.explain: Passive recon relies entirely on third parties that already hold the data — WHOIS registrars, public DNS resolvers, CT log mirrors, search engines — so nothing is sent directly to the target's own infrastructure.

questions.q: Why is a Certificate Transparency (CT) log such a valuable source for subdomain discovery?
options: It is a private database only the target organization can query
It lists every password ever used on the target's web applications
It is a public, append-only log of every TLS certificate issued, so every subdomain anyone requested a cert for is searchable
It only contains information about expired domains
questions.explain: Browsers require CAs to log every issued certificate to public CT logs. Searching one (e.g. via crt.sh) surfaces subdomains like staging. or vpn. without ever querying the target's own DNS servers.

questions.q: A DNS TXT record containing an SPF string is useful during passive recon because it:
options: Lists the IP ranges authorized to send mail for the domain, revealing mail infrastructure
Contains the target's internal Active Directory password policy
Reveals the physical address of the target's data center
Shows every employee's email password in plaintext
questions.explain: SPF records are published specifically so mail servers can validate senders, which means they double as a free, public list of a domain's authorized mail-sending IP ranges.

questions.q: Why can a job posting be a genuinely useful passive reconnaissance source?
options: Job postings are only useful for salary research, not technical recon
Recruiters intentionally publish a company's internal vulnerability scan results
Job boards require authentication, making them an active recon source
Postings written to attract qualified applicants often describe the real tech stack — cloud provider, orchestration tools, IaC, SIEM — in detail
questions.explain: A listing asking for "Kubernetes on AWS EKS, Terraform, and Splunk" experience hands you the cloud provider, orchestration layer, infrastructure-as-code tool, and SIEM, entirely through a public third-party site.

questions.q: Finding a world-readable S3 bucket through a Google dork like site:s3.amazonaws.com "target-company" is:
options: Impossible, since Google never indexes cloud storage URLs
A passive discovery technique, since the search happens against Google's index rather than the bucket directly
Only valid once the active-testing window of the engagement has formally opened
Automatically a violation of the rules of engagement in every case
questions.explain: The discovery itself runs against a search engine's already-indexed data, keeping it passive; any further access to the bucket's contents would then need to follow the engagement's evidence-handling and scope rules.
